sentences.text: Through traffic doesn’t use the inshore traffic zone when it can safely use the lane next to it.
The inshore zone is for local traffic.
But there are exceptions, and you’re one of them.
Vessels of less than twenty meters, sailing vessels, and vessels engaged in fishing may use the inshore zone.
So may any vessel going to or from a place inside it, or avoiding immediate danger.
A vessel of less than twenty meters, or a sailing vessel, shall not impede the safe passage of a power-driven vessel following a lane.
And a vessel engaged in fishing shall not impede any vessel following a lane.
It’s the same idea as Rule nine: small boats, sailboats and fishing boats stay out of the big ships’ way.
Avoid anchoring in a scheme, or near its ends.
And if you’re not using the scheme, avoid it by as wide a margin as practicable.
In a narrow channel: keep right, don’t impede, don’t cross in front of a ship, and don’t anchor.
On the rivers, downbound with a following current is in charge.
In a traffic scheme, merge at a small angle, cross at a right angle, and leave the lanes to the ships.
Next time, we’ll take up the first of the steering rules: sailing vessels meeting each other, and what the rules mean by overtaking.
